100:         )
101: 
102:     # Check monotonicity
103:     if not np.all(reference_timestamps[1:] - reference_timestamps[:-1] >= 0):
104:         raise ValueError("Reference timestamps are not monotonically increasing!")
105:     if not np.all(estimated_timestamps[1:] - estimated_timestamps[:-1] >= 0):
106:         raise ValueError("Estimated timestamps are not monotonically increasing!")
107: 
108:     # Check positivity (need for correct PCS metric calculation)
109:     if not np.all(reference_timestamps >= 0):
110:         raise ValueError("Reference timestamps can not be below 0!")
111:     if not np.all(estimated_timestamps >= 0):
112:         raise ValueError("Estimated timestamps can not be below 0!")
113: 
114: 
115: def absolute_error(reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps):
116:     """Compute the absolute deviations between estimated and reference timestamps,
117:     and then returns the median and average over all events
118: 
119:     Examples
120:     --------
121:     >>> reference_timestamps = mir_eval.io.load_events('reference.txt')
122:     >>> estimated_timestamps = mir_eval.io.load_events('estimated.txt')
123:     >>> mae, aae = mir_eval.align.absolute_error(reference_onsets, estimated_timestamps)
124: 
125:     Parameters
126:     ----------
127:     reference_timestamps : np.ndarray
128:         reference timestamps, in seconds
129:     estimated_timestamps : np.ndarray
130:         estimated timestamps, in seconds
131: 
132:     Returns
133:     -------
134:     mae : float
135:         Median absolute error
136:     aae: float
137:         Average absolute error
138:     """
139:     validate(reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps)
140:     deviations = np.abs(reference_timestamps - estimated_timestamps)
141:     return np.median(deviations), np.mean(deviations)
142: 
143: 
144: def percentage_correct(reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps, window=0.3):
145:     """Compute the percentage of correctly predicted timestamps. A timestamp is predicted
146:     correctly if its position doesn't deviate more than the window parameter from the ground
147:     truth timestamp.
148: 
149:     Examples
150:     --------
151:     >>> reference_timestamps = mir_eval.io.load_events('reference.txt')
152:     >>> estimated_timestamps = mir_eval.io.load_events('estimated.txt')
153:     >>> pc = mir_eval.align.percentage_correct(reference_onsets, estimated_timestamps, window=0.2)
154: 
155:     Parameters
156:     ----------
157:     reference_timestamps : np.ndarray
158:         reference timestamps, in seconds
159:     estimated_timestamps : np.ndarray
160:         estimated timestamps, in seconds
161:     window : float
162:         Window size, in seconds
163:         (Default value = .3)
164: 
165:     Returns
166:     -------
167:     pc : float
168:         Percentage of correct timestamps
169:     """
170:     validate(reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps)
171:     deviations = np.abs(reference_timestamps - estimated_timestamps)
172:     return np.mean(deviations <= window)
173: 
174: 
175: def percentage_correct_segments(
176:     reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps, duration: Optional[float] = None
177: ):
178:     """Calculate the percentage of correct segments (PCS) metric.
179: 
180:     It constructs segments out of predicted and estimated timestamps separately
181:     out of each given timestamp vector and calculates the percentage of overlap between correct
182:     segments compared to the total duration.
183: 
184:     WARNING: This metrics behaves differently depending on whether "duration" is given!
185: 
186:     If duration is not given (default case), the computation follows the MIREX lyrics alignment
187:     challenge 2020. For a timestamp vector with entries (t1,t2, ... tN), segments with
188:     the following (start, end) boundaries are created: (t1, t2), ... (tN-1, tN).
189:     After the segments are created, the overlap between the reference and estimated segments is
190:     determined and divided by the total duration, which is the distance between the
191:     first and last timestamp in the reference.
192: 
193:     If duration is given, the segment boundaries are instead (0, t1), (t1, t2), ... (tN, duration).
194:     The overlap is computed in the same way, but then divided by the duration parameter given to
195:     this function.
196:     This method follows the original paper [#fujihara2011] more closely, where the metric was
197:     proposed.
198:     As a result, this variant of the metrics punishes cases where the first estimated timestamp
199:     is too early or the last estimated timestamp is too late, whereas the MIREX variant does not.
200:     On the other hand, the MIREX metric is invariant to how long the eventless beginning and end
201:     parts of the audio are, which might be a desirable property.
202: 
203:     Examples
204:     --------
205:     >>> reference_timestamps = mir_eval.io.load_events('reference.txt')
206:     >>> estimated_timestamps = mir_eval.io.load_events('estimated.txt')
207:     >>> pcs = mir_eval.align.percentage_correct_segments(reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps)
208: 
209:     Parameters
210:     ----------
211:     reference_timestamps : np.ndarray
212:         reference timestamps, in seconds
213:     estimated_timestamps : np.ndarray
214:         estimated timestamps, in seconds
215:     duration : float
216:         Optional. Total duration of audio (seconds). WARNING: Metric is computed differently
217:         depending on whether this is provided or not - see documentation above!
218: 
219:     Returns
220:     -------
221:     pcs : float
222:         Percentage of time where ground truth and predicted segments overlap
223:     """
224:     validate(reference_timestamps, estimated_timestamps)
225:     if duration is not None:
226:         duration = float(duration)
227:         if duration <= 0:
228:             raise ValueError(
229:                 f"Positive duration needs to be provided, but got {duration}"
230:             )
231:         if np.max(reference_timestamps) > duration:
232:             raise ValueError(
233:                 "Expected largest reference timestamp"
234:                 f"{np.max(reference_timestamps)} to not be "
235:                 f"larger than duration {duration}"
236:             )
237:         if np.max(estimated_timestamps) > duration:
238:             raise ValueError(
239:                 "Expected largest estimated timestamp "
240:                 f"{np.max(estimated_timestamps)} to not be "
241:                 f"larger than duration {duration}"
242:             )
243: 
244:         ref_starts = np.concatenate([[0], reference_timestamps])
245:         ref_ends = np.concatenate([reference_timestamps, [duration]])
246:         est_starts = np.concatenate([[0], estimated_timestamps])
247:         est_ends = np.concatenate([estimated_timestamps, [duration]])
248:     else:
249:         # MIREX lyrics alignment 2020 style:
250:         # Ignore regions before start and after end reference timestamp
251:         duration = reference_timestamps[-1] - reference_timestamps[0]
252:         if duration <= 0:
253:             raise ValueError(
254:                 f"Reference timestamps are all identical, can not compute PCS"
255:                 f" metric!"
